sentences.text: This is the criminal revision petition u/s 397 Cr.PC filed by revisionists against the impugned order dated 20.10.2018 passed by Ld. MM (Mahila Court)-02, West, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi whereby the Ld. MM took cognizance of the offences punishable u/s 498A/406/34 IPC and ordered to summon the accused persons/revisionists.

entities.text: MM (Mahila Court)-02, West, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. I have heard arguments on the present revision petition and perused the record.
3. As per the impugned order dated 20.10.2018, Ld. MM took cognizance of the offences and supplied copy to revisionist Bhupender Negi and issued summons to the remaining accused persons.

4. Revisionists have argued that complainant/respondent no.2 Neema Negi left the matrimonial house in Hari Nagar, Delhi on 03.05.2015 and complainant Neema Negi was in the matrimonial house in Hari Nagar, Delhi, in the matrimonial house in Pune and in her parent's house in Ghaziabad, U.P for the period 18.02.2015 to 02.05.2015.

It is also stated that Neema Negi filed her complaint before CAW cell, East on 05/06.08.2015 and her complaint was with regard to the period 18.02.2015 to 02.05.2015.
5.

It is also stated by the revisionists that investigation report in this matter was submitted in September 2018 and cognizance of the alleged offences was taken by the concerned Ld. MM vide impugned order dated 20.10.2018.

sentences.text: Page no. 2 of 5 6.

It is also stated by the revisionists that cognizance of the alleged offences was taken after the lapse of three years since complainant Neema left the matrimonial house on 03.05.2015 and thus, the cognizance vide impugned order was time barred.
7. It is further stated by the revisionists that neither application for condonation of delay was filed nor delay was formally condoned by Ld. MM prior to taking cognizance.
8. It has been submitted by the revisionists that taking of cognizance of alleged offences by Ld MM vide impugned order may be set aside as the cognizance is time barred.

9. In support of their contentions, the revisionists have relied upon certain judgments i.e. judgment titled as State of Punjab vs Sarwan Singh, 1981 SCALE (1) 619 passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 02.04.1981, judgment titled as Sanapareddy Maheedhar & Anr. Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh,
Appeal (Crl.) 1708 of 2007 dated 13.12.2007, judgment titled as Rajani Kanta Padhi Vs. State of Orissa and Ors, Criminal Misc. Case No. 10215 of 2001 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Orissa.
10.On the other hand

sentences.text:
Ld. Addl.
PP has also argued that the law is well settled to the effect that the provision of Section 468 Cr.P.C which puts bar of limitation, cannot be extended to matrimonial offences specially where the allegations are of cruelty, torture and assault by the husband and other members of the family.
Ld Addl. PP for the State also argued that in the matter before Trial Court offence u/s 406 IPC is involved and it is a continuing offence and he argued that there is no illegality in impugned order.
11.I have heard the rival submissions and perused the record carefully.
Perusal of the record reveals that the marriage between the revisionist no. 1 and respondent no. 2 took place on 17.02.2015 and the respondent no. 2 started residing separately w.e.f 02.05.2015.
In her complaint, the complainant/respondent no.2 has leveled allegations of cruelty and demand of dowry at the hands of accused persons/revisionists in the month of April 2015.

Perusal of the record further reveals that respondent no. 2 filed complaint before CAW cell on 04.08.2015 and after inquiry by CAW cell, the FIR was registered on 05.11.2016 and after the completion of investigation, charge-sheet was filed before Ld. MM on 05.09.2018 and Ld. MM took cognizance of the offences vide impugned order on 20.10.2018.

12.Perusal of the record reveals that certain legal questions are involved as to whether the chargesheet is time barred Crl. Rev. No. 382/2018 Bhupender Negi & Ors. vs State & Anr. Page no. 4 of 5 or otherwise and as to whether the offences are continuing offences for which the Ld. MM was required to pass a reasoned order showing reasons for taking cognizance of offences as the offence was allegedly committed in the month of April 2015 and the cognizance of offence was taken vide impugned order dated 20.10.2018.

sentences.text: 13.I am of the opinion that Ld MM was required to hear the parties on the point of limitation and to pass a reasoned order on the aspect of cognizance.

14.In view of the aforesaid discussion, the order dated 20.10.2018 passed by Ld. MM is set aside and Ld. MM shall hear both the parties on the point of limitation and then to pass a reasoned order on the aspect of cognizance.
15.With the aforesaid observation, the Criminal Revision Petition is disposed of accordingly.
16.File of revision petition be consigned to Record Room after completing necessary formalities.
17.Trial Court Record be sent back to the concerned Court.
18.Copy of this order be sent to the concerned Ld. Trial Court.
MANISH by MANISH
